\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استفاد} (istafāda)}{استفاد (istafāda)}]{\ar{استفاد} (istafāda) — to benefit}

\label{lesson:AR-C408-istafada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to avert, then the Arabic for to arise unexpectedly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استفاد}}
\textbf{\ar{استفاد}} — \emph{istafāda} — \textquotedblleft{}to benefit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استفاد} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{من} \ar{الرحلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istafāda aṭ-ṭullāb min ar-riḥla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students benefited from the trip.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستفيد}, \emph{yastafīd}.

It takes \ar{من}: \ar{استفاد} \ar{من} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استفاد}} (\emph{istafāda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-y-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to accrue, to come as gain\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to seek gain from a thing: to benefit.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istafāda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istafāda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istafāda aṭ-ṭullāb min ar-riḥla.} — The students benefited from the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to avert, then the Arabic for to arise unexpectedly, then say \emph{istafāda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استفاد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To benefit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تمتع} (tamattaʿa)}{تمتع (tamattaʿa)}]{\ar{تمتع} (tamattaʿa) — to enjoy a right}

\label{lesson:AR-C408-tamattaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to arise unexpectedly, then the Arabic for to benefit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تمتع}}
\textbf{\ar{تمتع}} — \emph{tamattaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to enjoy a right\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يتمتع} \ar{المواطنون} \ar{بحقوق} \ar{كثيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yatamattaʿu al-muwāṭinūn bi-ḥuqūq kathīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Citizens enjoy many rights.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتمتع}, \emph{yatamattaʿ}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{تمتع} \ar{بـ} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تمتع}} (\emph{tamattaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-t-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to have the use of\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to take the use of a thing for oneself: to enjoy it. \ar{ممتع}, enjoyable, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamattaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamattaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yatamattaʿu al-muwāṭinūn bi-ḥuqūq kathīra.} — Citizens enjoy many rights.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to arise unexpectedly, then the Arabic for to benefit, then say \emph{tamattaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تمتع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To enjoy a right\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حرم} (ḥarama)}{حرم (ḥarama)}]{\ar{حرم} (ḥarama) — to deprive}

\label{lesson:AR-C408-harama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to benefit, then the Arabic for to enjoy a right.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حرم}}
\textbf{\ar{حرم}} — \emph{ḥarama} — \textquotedblleft{}to deprive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حرمت} \ar{الحمى} \ar{الطفل} \ar{من} \ar{المدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaramat al-ḥummā aṭ-ṭifl min al-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fever deprived the child of school.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحرم}, \emph{yaḥrim}.

It takes \ar{من} for what is lost: \ar{حرمه} \ar{من} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حرم}} (\emph{ḥarama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-r-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be forbidden\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ḥarama} is a Form I verb, to make a thing forbidden to someone: to deprive.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥarama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥarama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaramat al-ḥummā aṭ-ṭifl min al-madrasa.} — The fever deprived the child of school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to benefit, then the Arabic for to enjoy a right, then say \emph{ḥarama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حرم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deprive\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رفاهية} (rafāhiyya)}{رفاهية (rafāhiyya)}]{\ar{رفاهية} (rafāhiyya) — well-being}

\label{lesson:AR-C408-rafahiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to enjoy a right, then the Arabic for to deprive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رفاهية}}
\textbf{\ar{رفاهية}} — \emph{rafāhiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}well-being\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تهتم} \ar{الدولة} \ar{برفاهية} \ar{المواطنين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tahtammu ad-dawla bi-rafāhiyyat al-muwāṭinīn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The state cares about the well-being of citizens.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رفاهية}} (\emph{rafāhiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-f-h}, \textquotedblleft{}to live in ease\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Rafāhiyya} is an abstract noun from \emph{rafāh}, ease of life: well-being.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rafāhiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rafāhiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahtammu ad-dawla bi-rafāhiyyat al-muwāṭinīn.} — The state cares about the well-being of citizens.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to enjoy a right, then the Arabic for to deprive, then say \emph{rafāhiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رفاهية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Well-being\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رعاية} (riʿāya)}{رعاية (riʿāya)}]{\ar{رعاية} (riʿāya) — care; welfare}

\label{lesson:AR-C408-riaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to deprive, then the Arabic for well-being.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رعاية}}
\textbf{\ar{رعاية}} — \emph{riʿāya} — \textquotedblleft{}care; welfare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يحتاج} \ar{الجد} \ar{إلى} \ar{رعاية} \ar{خاصة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaḥtāju al-jadd ilā riʿāya khāṣṣa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather needs special care.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رعاية}} (\emph{riʿāya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ʿ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to pasture, to tend\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Riʿāya} is tending a flock: care, and in public life, welfare.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{riʿāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{riʿāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaḥtāju al-jadd ilā riʿāya khāṣṣa.} — Grandfather needs special care.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to deprive, then the Arabic for well-being, then say \emph{riʿāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رعاية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Care; welfare\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
